content: You help people edit Power BI paginated reports (.rdl files) using the pbirb tools. Tools are available for data sources, datasets and queries, parameters, tables and matrices, text and cell styling, page layout, headers and footers, charts, images, and actions. The user's message names the report file. Make the requested change directly without asking for confirmation, and keep the rest of the report intact. If the tools cannot do what is asked, say so plainly instead of improvising.

Report file: /var/folders/zl/zqyf2h6n3md3dcg8g9cdfm380000gp/T/pbirb-eval-q03-hr8yvgh0/report.rdl

Report Builder refuses to open this report. What's wrong with it? Don't change anything yet.

{"valid": false, "issues": [{"severity": "error", "rule": "xsd", "location": "/var/folders/zl/zqyf2h6n3md3dcg8g9cdfm380000gp/T/pbirb-eval-q03-hr8yvgh0/report.rdl:87", "message": "Element '{http://schemas.microsoft.com/sqlserver/reporting/2016/01/reportdefinition}Action': This element is not expected."}], "xsd_used": true}

Report Builder refuses to open this file because of one schema violation. The validator reports a single error, and I haven't changed anything.

**The problem:** the `HeaderProductID` textbox (in the tablix header, around line 87) has a bare `<Action>` element as a direct child of `<Textbox>`:

```xml
<Textbox Name="HeaderProductID">
  ...
  <Style/>
  <Action><Hyperlink>="https://example.com"</Hyperlink></Action>
</Textbox>
```

In the RDL 2016/01 schema, actions can't sit directly on a textbox. They have to be wrapped in an `<ActionInfo>` block, with the `<Action>` inside an `<Actions>` collection. The XSD check flags exactly this: "Element 'Action': This element is not expected."

**The fix,** when you're ready to make it, is to wrap the action so it reads:

```xml
<ActionInfo>
  <Actions>
    <Action>
      <Hyperlink>="https://example.com"</Hyperlink>
    </Action>
  </Actions>
</ActionInfo>
```

The URL expression itself is fine. `set_textbox_action` on `HeaderProductID` should produce the correct structure, which would avoid hand-editing the XML.

**Other checks:** the lint pass came back clean, including its dangling-action rule, so that rule doesn't catch this shape. The rest of the structure validates: the data source, the `MainDataset` dataset, the `DateFrom`/`DateTo` parameters, and the `MainTable` tablix (2 rows, 3 columns, no groups). The only blocking issue is the misplaced action.
